reasons: Only sections one to nine were reviewed, out of twenty-nine.

terms.meaning: The automatic check that decides whether a release is allowed to go out.
A saved set of earlier scores that new results are compared against.
The amount a score may fall before it counts as a regression.
The written guide a judge uses to score a result, with anchored examples for each score level.
A short code computed from a file's contents, which changes whenever the contents change.
The automated scorer that grades results against the rubric.
A measurable drop in quality compared with the baseline.

depends_on: a baseline file in a temporary folder during tests
used_by: pytest (runs the test file directly; no other callers visible)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Gate properties and setup
sections.what: States the three properties the gate must keep, and imports the gate module from the evals folder.
sections.why: Sets out what the tests protect.
sections.watch_out: The import runs the gate's top-level code during test collection.

sections.name: score_set
sections.title: Full score set builder
sections.what: Builds a complete set of five dimension scores, all set to four unless the test overrides some.
sections.why: Gives each test a valid, complete set of scores.
sections.watch_out: The dimension names come from the gate, so renaming one there changes this helper's output.

sections.name: graded_case
sections.title: Graded case builder
sections.what: Builds a graded case result from a set of scores, with a justification long enough to pass review and a weighted score averaged from the values.
sections.why: Lets tests create realistic case results cheaply.
sections.watch_out: The justification is padded filler, so these tests do not check the real length rule.

sections.name: report_with
sections.title: Report builder
sections.what: Builds a report holding the grades it is given.
sections.why: Gives tests a report to pass to the gate functions.
sections.watch_out: None apparent.

sections.name: baseline
sections.title: Baseline fixture
sections.what: Redirects the baseline path into a temporary folder and provides a helper that writes a baseline file with a rubric fingerprint and judge model.
sections.why: So the tests never touch the real baseline file.
sections.watch_out: The default fingerprint is computed from the current rubric files, so editing a rubric changes what the helper writes.

sections.name: TestSkippedIsNotPassed
sections.title: Skipped cases are not passes
sections.what: Checks that skipped cases are excluded from failures and shown as skipped, that ungraded cases are not averaged in as zeros, and that a report with no graded cases gives no means.
sections.why: Prevents skipped work from reading as a pass, or as a drop in quality.
sections.watch_out: The averaging rule is what protects this; changing the averaging reopens the problem.

sections.name: TestBaselineComparison
sections.title: Baseline comparison
sections.what: Checks that no baseline means nothing is compared, that a drop within tolerance passes, that a drop beyond tolerance is reported with its size, that improvements are never reported, that a dimension missing from the baseline is skipped, and that several regressions are all listed.
sections.why: Defines what counts as a regression.
sections.watch_out: The tests assume a particular tolerance value from the gate, so changing that value changes which drops pass.

sections.name: TestIncomparabilityIsNotRegression
sections.title: Changed judge or rubric is not a regression
sections.what: Checks that a changed rubric text or a changed judge model is reported as not comparable or as a judge change, rather than as a regression in the system under test.
sections.why: A moved yardstick is a different problem from a shrunken result, and the report should say so.
sections.watch_out: The rubric fingerprint must change whenever the rubric text changes, or this check fails silently.

sections.name: TestRubricsOnDisk
sections.title: Rubric file rules
sections.what: Checks that all five dimensions have a rubric, that each rubric has anchored text at levels one, three, and five with at least twenty-five words each, that written justification is required with at least twenty words, and that known biases are documented.
sections.why: Likely reason: the middle anchor is required because judges tend to cluster in the middle when it is left undefined. The rest of the reason is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Word counts are a crude check, so long but vague anchor text would pass.

sections.name: TestGoldenCasesOnDisk
sections.title: Checks on the golden example cases
sections.what: Confirms the golden folder holds exactly four example cases, that none of their reference answers was produced by software, that one pair of shared capabilities appears in the right two cases, and that the sparse-evidence case has only one evidence item with high authority.
sections.why: The reference answers must be written by people, otherwise the test grades the software against its own output. The other checks guard the example inputs against quiet changes.
sections.watch_out: Adding or removing a golden case changes the expected count of four, so this test fails until the count is updated on purpose.

sections.name: TestJudgePrompt
sections.title: Checks on the text sent to the judge
sections.what: Confirms that case-specific notes appear in the judge's instructions only when given, that both the reference answer and the candidate answer reach the judge, that rubric bias notes reach it, and that the judge model name is fixed to one exact version.
sections.why: The judge is the model that scores answers, so it must receive the right material. The model name is pinned so scores do not change silently when a different model is used.
sections.watch_out: Changing the pinned judge model name changes the scores, and this test fails until that change is made deliberately.

sections.name: a_record
sections.title: Sample record helper for tests
sections.what: Builds one sample process record by calling the shared fixture helper, so many tests can start from a valid example without repeating the setup.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond its use as shared setup. It also adds the repository root to the import path before loading the fixture.
sections.watch_out: Every test that uses this helper inherits any change made to the fixture helper.

sections.name: a_case
sections.title: Temporary case folder helper
sections.what: Creates an industry and case folder inside a temporary location for a test to read or write.
sections.why: Gives checks a real folder structure while keeping the real repository untouched.
sections.watch_out: Files written here are cleared after the test, so nothing from these tests persists for inspection.

sections.name: TestCitationsResolveAtAnyDepth
sections.title: Checks that citations resolve
sections.what: Confirms that evidence ids are found however deeply they are nested, including the single-id form used on challenges, and that empty citations are ignored. Also confirms that a citation missing from the evidence pack fails the gate, while a record whose citations are all in the pack passes.
sections.why: A citation that points at nothing would look like support. Every citation has to match an item in the pack.
sections.watch_out: If the key name used for evidence ids in the record is renamed, these checks will stop finding citations and may pass wrongly.

sections.name: TestEvidenceCoverage
sections.title: Checks on evidence coverage
sections.what: Confirms a complete record passes, that a missing confidence entry for a part of the record fails, and that a part with no evidence but a score above zero fails.
sections.why: Confidence should come from evidence, not from a number the system declares about itself.
sections.watch_out: The missing-entry check depends on the framing part being one of the named parts, so renaming a part changes what is tested.

sections.name: TestParameterBounds (part 1)
sections.title: Checks on value ranges
sections.what: Confirms a well-formed set of value inputs passes, that a range whose low figure is above its high figure fails, and that a share above one fails.
sections.why: An inverted range would flip the downside and upside estimates, and a share above one is not a real share.
sections.watch_out: The share limit applies only to fields that are shares. Widening it would let impossible values through.

sections.name: TestParameterBounds: test_an_unbounded_range_is_not_forced_into_zero_to_one
sections.title: Unbounded ranges are allowed
sections.what: Confirms that effort in full-time staff and the adoption period in months can take large values and still pass, because they are counts or durations, not shares.
sections.why: Forcing these into zero to one would reject every real record. The test is there so that a future clamp is not added by mistake.
sections.watch_out: Adding a zero-to-one limit to these fields would fail every real record.

sections.name: TestEffortShares
sections.title: Checks on effort shares
sections.what: Confirms that step shares of the process add up to one and pass. A set that does not add up fails under its own check name.
sections.why: Derived figures are only correct when the shares total one.
sections.watch_out: The share-sum check and the share warning are separate checks, so they must keep distinct names or one run reports the same check twice.

sections.name: TestNoTotalsOnAgentPaths
sections.title: No totals on agent output
sections.what: Confirms the agent layer as it stands has no money or value total fields. Also confirms that a planted total field in a scratch copy of the agent folder is caught.
sections.why: Totals must come from the value engine, not from language model output, so figures cannot be invented by agents.
sections.watch_out: The check reads the folder under the repository root it is given, so changing that root changes what is inspected.

sections.name: TestTheCandidatePathIsReal
sections.title: Candidate records are freshly generated
sections.what: Confirms the gate runs the pipeline itself to create candidate records for every case. Also confirms that a pipeline crash is reported as a failure, not a skip.
sections.why: An old record file could pass checks while describing code that no longer exists, so fresh generation is required and a crash must not look like a pass.
sections.watch_out: If the pipeline error is caught and reported as a skip, this test should fail. Do not hide errors silently.

sections.name: TestArithmeticOnAgentPaths
sections.title: Arithmetic on value figures in agents
sections.what: Confirms that a multiplication producing a value figure inside an agent is caught, and that ordinary counting arithmetic such as adding one to an index is left alone.
sections.why: A total could hide inside a calculation with no named field, so the check also reads the arithmetic. Counting is allowed so the check is not switched off.
sections.watch_out: Making the check stricter could flag normal counting and lead people to disable it.

sections.name: TestTheSchemaCheckLooksAtThisRunsRecord
sections.title: Schema check reads this run's record
sections.what: Confirms that a missing record causes the schema checks to skip rather than read an old file, that a good record passes, and that the two share checks have different names.
sections.why: An earlier version reported passes from stale output while the pipeline was broken, and reported one check twice with different results.
sections.watch_out: A skip must never turn into a pass. This test guards that boundary.

sections.name: TestTheValuePurityGate
sections.title: Value purity gate
sections.what: Confirms that a clean value folder passes, that a direct import of the model library fails, that an indirect import through another module also fails, and that the real value folder is clean with nothing skipped.
sections.why: Value figures must be computed without language models. An indirect route to a model is as harmful as a direct one.
sections.watch_out: The check depends on folder names and module paths. Moving the value or agents folder means the check must be reviewed.

sections.name: TestDeclaredPrerequisitesMustBeEvidenced (part 1)
sections.title: Prerequisite check setup
sections.what: Provides helpers that build a sample assumption and a sample record containing it, so later tests can check whether each declared prerequisite has evidence behind it.
sections.why: A prerequisite with no evidence is an unproven claim. The helpers skip normal validation on purpose so a deliberately broken record can be tested.
sections.watch_out: Records built this way bypass the schema's own checks, so a passing test here does not prove the schema would accept that record.

sections.name: TestDeclaredPrerequisitesMustBeEvidenced: test_an_unnamed_prerequisite_fails
sections.title: Prerequisite evidence rules
sections.what: Confirms that an unnamed prerequisite fails, that an assumption marked unsupported may cite nothing and still pass, and that a citation outside the case's evidence pack fails. A missing payload skips the check rather than failing it.
sections.why: An honest unsupported answer has to be allowed, or the system leaves no honest way to admit a gap. The missing payload is already reported by another check, so reporting it twice would point at the wrong file.
sections.watch_out: Requiring citations on unsupported items would remove the only honest way to state a gap.

sections.name: TestDeclaredPrerequisitesMustBeEvidenced: test_a_record_with_no_assumptions_passes
sections.title: Empty assumptions and the real lending case
sections.what: Confirms that a record with no assumptions passes. Also confirms that the real lending case passes and cites the evidence item stating that the platform has no synchronous write path.
sections.why: The lending case is the one that exposed the defect, so it is kept as a real regression test.
sections.watch_out: This test depends on both the generated candidate and the golden input, so a change to either can break it for reasons unrelated to the check.

sections.name: TestTheCaseInputContract (part 1)
sections.title: Case input contract setup and first checks
sections.what: Provides helpers that write a case input file to a temporary folder and load the real lending input. Confirms a valid case passes, a misspelt depth tier fails at the gate, and an inverted volume range fails at the gate.
sections.why: Input errors should be caught at the gate, before a long run fails partway through.
sections.watch_out: Changing the real lending input file changes what these tests start from.

sections.name: TestTheCaseInputContract: test_the_error_names_the_case_not_just_the_field
sections.title: Input errors name the case
sections.what: Confirms a failed input check names the case it belongs to, that a case placed in the wrong industry folder is reported, and that a case that fails validation skips the later enabler check rather than reporting it as passed.
sections.why: Reporting the enabler check as passed for a file that was never read would be a false pass.
sections.watch_out: The folder name must match the industry in the case, so moving a case folder can trigger this check.

sections.name: TestEveryBlockerIsNamedAtOnce
sections.title: All blockers reported together
sections.what: Confirms that a case which cannot be scored lists every blocker at once: the unwritten reference, the missing candidate output, and the missing judge key. Also confirms the missing key is named by its variable, and that the live golden set currently reports the unwritten references and the missing judge key.
sections.why: Showing only the first blocker forced several slow fix-and-rerun rounds. The live-set test records the current state of the repository.
sections.watch_out: The live-set test will fail once references are written or a judge key is added, so it must be updated then.

summary: Tests the quality gate's logic, so the gate can be trusted to decide whether a release ships. Only the first nine sections were reviewed here.
purpose: Tests the gate in the evals runner: how skipped cases are counted, how scores are compared with a saved baseline, how judge or rubric changes are reported, and whether the rubric files meet their rules.
why: The gate decides whether a release ships, so its arithmetic needs the same testing as the code it grades. The file header names three properties that matter most.
how: Helpers build sample case grades and reports. A fixture redirects the baseline file to a temporary folder. Tests check that skipped cases are not counted as passes, that regressions beyond tolerance are reported, that changes to the judge or rubric are reported as not comparable, and that each rubric has the required anchors and fields.
inputs: Sample scores and reports built in the test file, a temporary baseline file, and the rubric files on disk.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest. The file writes only to a temporary folder.
risks: The file imports the runner directly, so changes to its top-level code run during test collection. The rubric word-count rules are crude and can be met by vague text.
debug: If a regression test fails, check the tolerance constant and the baseline values. If a rubric test fails, open the rubric file it names. If a rubric fingerprint test fails, a rubric has changed and the baseline may need regenerating.
